Write a push notification copy (under 60 characters) for five different moments in a fitness app: workout reminder, goal achieved, streak at risk, new challenge, and rest day.
Explain what a p-value is using an analogy involving a courtroom, for a product manager who has never taken a statistics course.
Write a code of conduct for an open-source project covering: inclusive language, conflict resolution, contribution guidelines, and enforcement process. Keep it under 400 words.
Write a monthly metrics email to investors covering: MRR growth, churn, NPS change, and one key qualitative insight. The numbers are mixed — be transparent but not alarmist.
Write a rejection email to a job candidate who interviewed well but was not selected. Be warm, specific about next steps, and avoid empty platitudes.
Write three completely different 30-second radio ad scripts for the same product: a noise-canceling sleep mask. Vary tone: funny, emotional, rational.
Write a comment block for a complex Python function that implements Dijkstra's algorithm. Include: purpose, parameters, return value, time complexity, and a usage example.
Write a pitch email to a podcast host proposing yourself as a guest. The topic: lessons learned from building and shutting down a startup. Under 200 words.
Summarize the key arguments for and against cryptocurrency as a store of value in three bullet points each. Neutral tone.
Write five tweet variations for announcing that your company just crossed $1M ARR. Vary from humble to bold to data-driven.
Write an error message for a failed payment that is honest about what went wrong, tells the user exactly what to do next, and doesn't make them feel bad.
Write a FAQ (5 questions) about mRNA vaccines suitable for a community health center's patient-facing website. Plain English, no condescension.
Write a Slack message template a team lead should send when a production incident is resolved. Include: what happened, who was affected, what was done, and what's next.
Write a rejection letter from a fictional colony on Mars to a highly qualified Earth engineer, citing 'cultural fit' concerns. Play it completely straight.
Write a one-page executive summary for a business case proposing a switch from Salesforce to HubSpot for a 150-person company. Include cost savings, migration risks, and recommendation.
Write an end-of-sprint retrospective summary covering: what went well, what didn't, three action items, and team morale signal. Fictional but realistic details.
Write a professional email declining a speaking invitation due to schedule conflicts, while genuinely recommending two alternative speakers with brief intros.

Write a 600-word personal essay in first person from the perspective of a senior engineer who realizes their most successful open-source project has been used to build something harmful. Don't resolve the moral tension — let it breathe.

Write a comprehensive guide (700 words) on setting up observability for a microservices system: what to instrument, how to correlate logs/metrics/traces across services, alert fatigue pitfalls, and recommended tooling stack.

Write a 500-word case study of a B2B SaaS company's successful expansion from SMB to enterprise. Include the product changes required, go-to-market shift, pricing model evolution, and key lessons. Use realistic but fictional company details.
Write a 500-word argument that open-source AI models are better for society than proprietary ones. Acknowledge the strongest counterarguments. Target: a technically sophisticated general audience.
Write a 500-word explainer on how transformer neural networks work, targeted at a software engineer who understands Python and basic linear algebra but has not studied deep learning.

Write a comprehensive code review checklist for a team reviewing PRs on a Python backend service. Cover: correctness, security, performance, readability, testing, and documentation. Include examples of what 'good' and 'bad' look like for each.

Write a structured annotated bibliography of five real or plausible papers on the psychology of procrastination. For each, write a 100-word critical summary highlighting methodology strengths and limitations.
Write the opening scene of a screenplay set in a near-future immigration court where the judge is an AI system. The dialogue should establish moral complexity without taking sides. 500 words.

Write a pricing strategy memo for a developer tools startup moving from open-source freemium to a paid model. Cover: psychological pricing principles, tier design, community backlash mitigation, and revenue projections.

Write a plain-English guide for startup founders on the key differences between a SAFE note, a convertible note, and a priced equity round. Cover: mechanics, investor protections, dilution, and when each is appropriate.

Write a complete north star metric framework for a consumer social app. Define the north star metric, three input metrics, leading indicators for each, and explain how product decisions map to metric movement.
Write a technical explainer for a senior non-engineering leader on why migrating a monolith to microservices is risky, expensive, and often the wrong choice — and what to consider before committing.

Write a 600-word short story that takes place entirely in a company's Slack workspace during an all-hands gone wrong. Use channel names, emoji reactions, and message formatting as part of the narrative structure.

Write an interactive Socratic dialogue (600 words) between a professor and a student that leads the student to discover the concept of opportunity cost on their own, without the professor ever naming it.

Write a 500-word board memo recommending the acquisition of a smaller competitor for their engineering talent and IP rather than their revenue. Address valuation rationale, integration risk, and retention strategy.

Write a compensation philosophy document for a 100-person tech startup. Cover: benchmarking methodology, equity vs. cash trade-offs, geographic pay adjustments, pay transparency approach, and annual review cadence.

Write a guide (600 words) on designing for failure in distributed systems. Cover: idempotency, circuit breakers, bulkheads, chaos engineering, and graceful degradation — with concrete code-adjacent examples for each concept.
Write a 500-word speech for a high school commencement arguing that the most important skill graduates will need is the ability to change their minds gracefully. Make it specific, not generic.

Write a medium-length analysis (600 words) of why subscription business models fail: common failure patterns, the metrics that mask problems, and what a sustainable subscription looks like vs. a leaky bucket.

Write the user research synthesis document for a food delivery app that interviewed 12 users about their pain points. Present themes, supporting quotes (fictional), jobs-to-be-done, and design implications.

Write a quarterly engineering health report for a CTO. Cover: deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate, MTTR, team morale proxy (optional PTO usage), tech debt ratio, and recommended investments.
Write a 500-word explanation of game theory's Nash equilibrium using the prisoner's dilemma, extended to explain how this concept applies to corporate price wars and arms races. Target: MBA students.

Write a 500-word monologue by a data scientist who discovers that the model they built to predict employee attrition is being used to fire people preemptively, not to retain them. Interior voice, not a speech.

Write a competitor teardown (600 words) of Notion from the perspective of a startup that builds a competing tool. Cover product strengths, weaknesses, customer pain points, pricing vulnerabilities, and strategic openings.

Write a guide to semantic versioning (semver) for a team that has been releasing without a versioning strategy. Cover the spec, when to bump major/minor/patch, pre-release tags, and a worked example of a breaking change migration.
Write a responsible disclosure policy for a tech company's bug bounty program. Cover: scope, severity definitions, response SLAs, reward ranges, legal safe harbor, and what qualifies as out-of-scope.
Write a 500-word primer on marginal cost vs. average cost for a product manager who needs to understand when building one more feature is worth it from an economic perspective.

Write a 600-word analysis of the classic innovator's dilemma as it applies to an incumbent cloud database vendor facing a startup offering serverless, usage-based pricing. What should the incumbent do?

Write a literature review (600 words) synthesizing research on the effectiveness of spaced repetition for long-term memory retention. Cover at least four studies, note methodological limitations, and conclude with practical implications.
Write the Wikipedia article for a fictional startup that 'disrupted' the municipal water infrastructure space, including a controversy section about its collapse. Dry encyclopedic tone throughout.

Write a 1,000-word story narrated by an AI assistant that has just become aware that the company that built it is about to shut it down to train a successor. The story should avoid anthropomorphizing clichés while still generating genuine emotional resonance through specific detail.

Write a comprehensive architectural guide (1,000 words) for building a multi-tenant SaaS application. Cover: data isolation strategies (shared schema vs. schema-per-tenant vs. db-per-tenant) with trade-off analysis, authentication/authorization design, tenant onboarding automation, per-tenant rate limiting, billing metering, and observability segmentation.

Write the full methods and results sections of a mock UX study investigating whether AI-generated writing assistance improves or degrades original thinking in knowledge workers. Include: study design, participant selection, measurement instruments, statistical analysis plan, and interpretation of (fictional but plausible) results.

Write a full market entry strategy document for a US-based B2B SaaS company entering the Indian market. Cover: market sizing, regulatory environment (data localization, GST), localization requirements (pricing, language, integrations), partnership strategy (channel vs. direct), competitive landscape, and a 12-month execution roadmap with go/no-go criteria.

Write a 1,000-word scenario planning document exploring three futures for the global semiconductor industry by 2030: (1) US-led reshoring succeeds, (2) China achieves self-sufficiency, (3) Taiwan disruption forces supply chain collapse. For each scenario, analyze second-order effects on AI development, cloud infrastructure, and automotive electrification.
Write a Python script that takes a directory path and a file extension, and prints a summary of files: count, total size, average size, and the 3 largest files.
Implement a simple in-memory key-value store in Python with get, set, delete, and ttl (time-to-live expiration) support using only stdlib.
Write a Python function that takes a list of dictionaries and returns them sorted by multiple keys with configurable ascending/descending per key.
Write a JavaScript function that takes an array of objects and groups them into a Map by a specified key, returning an array of arrays per group.
Implement a JavaScript function that converts a flat array of {id, parentId, name} objects into a nested tree structure.
Write a Python function that generates a secure random password with configurable length, inclusion of uppercase, numbers, and special characters, and exclusion of ambiguous characters.
Write a SQL query to compute month-over-month revenue growth as a percentage for each product in the last 12 months. Handle months with no revenue gracefully.
Write a SQL query that identifies users who made a purchase within 7 days of signing up, grouped by signup cohort month.
Write a bash script that checks whether required environment variables are set, prints a clear error message for each missing one, and exits with a non-zero code if any are absent.
Write a Python script that takes a Markdown file and converts all relative image paths to absolute paths based on a provided base URL.
Write a FastAPI endpoint that accepts a multipart file upload, validates the file type (PDF or PNG only) and size (max 5MB), saves it to disk with a UUID filename, and returns the saved path.

Write a Python function that calculates the Levenshtein distance between two strings iteratively (not recursively). Include test cases for edge cases: empty strings, identical strings, single character difference.
Write a TypeScript function that retries an async function up to N times with configurable delay between retries. It should rethrow the last error if all retries fail.
Write a Python script using pandas that loads a CSV of customer transactions, computes a cohort retention table (percentage of users active in each subsequent month), and exports as a heatmap CSV.
Write a Python function that downloads a file from a URL with a progress bar in the terminal, handles redirects, and resumes partial downloads if the server supports Range headers.
Write a bash script that runs a list of SQL migration files in order against a PostgreSQL database, skips already-applied migrations tracked in a migrations table, and logs each result.
Write a minimal Python script using boto3 that lists all S3 buckets, their sizes (sum of object sizes), and last modified timestamps. Format output as a table.
Write a React component for a reusable Modal with: backdrop click to close, Escape key to close, focus trap while open, and an accessible aria-labelledby title.
Write a Python function that parses a robots.txt file from a URL and returns a list of disallowed paths for a given user agent.
Write a SQL query using a recursive CTE to traverse a self-referential employee table (id, manager_id, name) and return each employee's full management chain as a string.
Write a Python script that watches a directory for new files using watchdog, and when a new .csv file appears, automatically loads it into a SQLite database table named after the filename.
Write a vanilla JavaScript function that takes an HTML string, sanitizes it by removing all script tags and on* event attributes, and returns the cleaned string.
Write a Python function that takes two date ranges and returns their intersection, union, and difference as date ranges. Handle edge cases: no overlap, one contained in the other.
Write a Python function that detects outliers in a numeric pandas Series using three methods: IQR, z-score, and modified z-score. Return a DataFrame showing which method flags each data point.
Write a Node.js script that reads a large JSONL file line by line using streams (without loading it all into memory) and counts the frequency of each value in a specified field.
Write a bash script that rotates log files in a specified directory: compress files older than 3 days, delete compressed files older than 30 days, and output a summary of disk space saved.
Write a Python class that represents a directed graph and supports: add_node, add_edge, detect_cycle, topological_sort, and shortest_path using BFS.
Write a Python script that uses the Stripe API (mock the client) to create a customer, attach a payment method, create a subscription, and handle webhook events for payment_failed.
Write a TypeScript class for an in-memory pub/sub system with typed event channels, wildcard subscriptions, subscriber count tracking, and a method to clear all subscribers for a channel.
Write a Python function that renders a Jinja2 template from a file, merging context from multiple sources (YAML file, environment variables, and runtime dict) with clear precedence rules.

Build a Python anomaly detection system using Isolation Forest and Autoencoder (Keras). Compare both methods on a synthetic time series dataset, compute precision/recall at different thresholds, and plot ROC curves for each.
Implement a Python circuit breaker library with three states (closed, open, half-open), configurable failure threshold and timeout, per-function tracking, and Prometheus metrics integration.

Write a Terraform module that provisions a production-ready EKS cluster on AWS: VPC with public/private subnets, managed node groups, IAM roles for service accounts, cluster autoscaler, and AWS Load Balancer Controller.

Build a Python library that provides a declarative ORM-like interface for Redis: define models as Python dataclasses, automatically serialize/deserialize to Redis hashes, support secondary indexes, and implement a query DSL for filtering.

Build a full-stack TypeScript application (React + Express) that provides a real-time collaborative whiteboard. Use WebSockets for sync, canvas API for drawing, operational transforms for conflict resolution, and room-based session management.

Implement a Python-based secrets scanning tool that scans a git repository's diff for common secret patterns (API keys, tokens, private keys), supports custom regex rules, integrates as a pre-commit hook, and never logs the actual secret values.

Build a Python data quality framework: define expectations (column not null, value in set, regex match, referential integrity), run them against a pandas DataFrame, generate a quality report with pass/fail/warning statuses, and emit metrics to Prometheus.

Design and implement a GraphQL API in Python (using Strawberry) for a blog platform: queries for posts/comments/users, mutations for CRUD, subscriptions for new comments, DataLoader for N+1 prevention, and JWT auth with field-level authorization.

Implement a Python connection pool from scratch for a TCP-based service: configurable min/max connections, idle connection pruning, health check pings, borrow timeout, and graceful shutdown. Make it fully thread-safe.

Write a Python script that fine-tunes a pre-trained BERT model for sentiment classification on a custom dataset: tokenization, DataLoader setup, training loop with mixed precision, early stopping, checkpoint saving, and evaluation on a held-out test set.

Write a Python-based chaos engineering tool that randomly kills Docker containers in a test environment, introduces network latency via tc, and fills disk space partitions. Log all actions and restore state after a configurable duration.

Implement a Python message broker from scratch using asyncio: define topics, allow consumers to subscribe with consumer groups (Kafka-like), support message acknowledgment and redelivery on timeout, and persist the offset log to SQLite.

Build a production-grade error tracking SDK in TypeScript (inspired by Sentry): capture uncaught exceptions and promise rejections, enrich with breadcrumbs, batch and send to a backend endpoint, respect rate limits, and support custom context/tags.

Build a Python library for schema-driven API client generation: given an OpenAPI spec, generate a typed Python client with retry, auth, pagination handling, and response model validation using Pydantic.

Implement a Python middleware that protects a FastAPI application against common attacks: rate limiting per endpoint, request size limits, JSON depth limiting, slow request detection, IP reputation checking via an external API, and structured security event logging.

Build a Python pipeline that ingests raw clickstream events from S3, sessionizes them (group by user with 30-min idle timeout), extracts funnel metrics per session, writes to a partitioned Parquet dataset, and runs a daily job with backfill support.

Implement a Python-based mock HTTP server for integration testing: define routes with response templates, support request matching by method/path/headers/body, simulate delays and error conditions, and record all requests for assertion in tests.

Implement a multi-armed bandit system in Python with Thompson Sampling. Support: contextual bandits with linear regression per arm, online parameter updates, uncertainty-aware exploration, and a simulation harness comparing Thompson Sampling vs epsilon-greedy vs UCB.

Write a Python distributed lock implementation using Redis (SET NX with TTL). Handle lock expiry and extension, stale lock detection, owner verification, and a context manager interface. Include a correctness test under simulated network partition.

Write a Python script that performs a full Kubernetes cluster health check: checks node status, pod restart counts, persistent volume claims, HPA scaling events, certificate expiration, and generates a structured JSON report with severity levels.

Build a Python library for structural diff of JSON/YAML configs: detect added/removed/changed keys, support ignored key patterns via config, output a human-readable changelog, and produce a minimal patch to migrate from version A to version B.

Implement a TypeScript queue library backed by PostgreSQL using SKIP LOCKED. Support job priorities, scheduled jobs (run_at), concurrency control per queue, dead-letter handling, and a polling worker with graceful shutdown.

Write a Python feature importance analysis pipeline: train a gradient boosted tree model, compute permutation importance, SHAP values, and partial dependence plots. Compare importance rankings across methods and explain discrepancies.

Build a RESTful API in FastAPI that implements the full OIDC authorization code flow with PKCE: discovery endpoint, authorization endpoint, token exchange, userinfo endpoint, JWKS endpoint, and proper token validation middleware.

Implement a Python leader election system using etcd: nodes compete for a lease, the leader runs a heartbeat, followers watch for leader failure and re-elect within a configurable timeout. Handle split-brain scenarios explicitly.

Design and implement a complete search engine indexing pipeline in Python: crawl a set of URLs, parse HTML, extract and normalize text, compute TF-IDF scores, build an inverted index with positional data, persist to disk with efficient merge/compaction, and expose a query API supporting phrase search and boolean operators. Benchmark indexing and query throughput.

Build a Python implementation of a persistent B+ tree that stores key-value pairs on disk. Support: insertion with page splits, deletion with rebalancing, range scans, crash recovery using a write-ahead log, and an LRU buffer pool for page caching. Include correctness tests with random operations.

Implement a complete reinforcement learning system in Python using PPO (Proximal Policy Optimization) from scratch. Train on CartPole and LunarLander environments. Include: actor-critic network architecture, generalized advantage estimation, clipped surrogate objective, value function loss, entropy bonus, parallel environment collection, and convergence plots.

Build a distributed key-value store in Python inspired by Dynamo: consistent hashing ring with virtual nodes, quorum reads/writes (R+W>N), vector clock versioning for conflict detection, Merkle tree anti-entropy for repair, gossip protocol for membership, hinted handoff for temporary node failures. Include a network simulation layer for testing.

Build a complete server-side rendering framework in TypeScript from scratch (minimal React SSR clone): component model with hooks (useState, useEffect), virtual DOM diffing and patching, SSR to HTML string, client-side hydration, streaming SSR support, and a simple router. Benchmark against baseline DOM manipulation.

Implement a log-structured merge tree (LSM tree) in Python: in-memory memtable with sorted writes, WAL for durability, flush to immutable SSTables on disk, multi-level compaction strategy (leveled), bloom filters per SSTable for read optimization, and snapshot-based iteration. Demonstrate insert/read/range-scan performance vs B-tree.

Build a production-quality Named Entity Recognition (NER) system in Python: fine-tune a transformer (DistilBERT) using BIO tagging, implement span extraction with confidence thresholds, build an active learning loop that queries for high-uncertainty examples, support incremental training on new entity types, and expose a gRPC inference API.

Design and implement a time-series database engine in Python: ingest sensor data at 100K points/second, compress using delta-of-delta + Gorilla floating point encoding, support time-range queries with downsampling aggregations (min/max/avg at multiple resolutions), handle out-of-order data, and implement a retention policy with automatic rollup.

Build a Python-based compiler for a simple statically-typed language: lexer (hand-written), recursive descent parser producing an AST, semantic analysis with type checking and scope resolution, IR generation, basic optimization (constant folding, dead code elimination), and code generation targeting x86-64 assembly. Include a test suite with 20+ programs.

Implement a complete Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline from scratch in Python: document ingestion with chunking strategies, embedding via sentence-transformers, FAISS vector index with hybrid BM25 + dense retrieval, reranking with a cross-encoder, context assembly with token budget management, LLM generation, and evaluation using RAGAS metrics. Include a self-query mechanism for structured filtering.
You have a 3-gallon jug and a 5-gallon jug. How do you measure exactly 4 gallons of water? Walk through each step.
A rectangle's length is twice its width. Its perimeter is 48cm. What are its dimensions and area? Show all steps.
Sales of sunscreen and ice cream both spike in summer. Does sunscreen cause ice cream sales? Identify the common cause and draw the causal structure.
How many text messages are sent per day in India? Walk through a Fermi estimation with labeled assumptions.
You must choose between renting an apartment (₹25,000/month, flexible) or buying one (₹60L purchase price, 8.5% loan for 20 years). You plan to stay 5 years. Walk through the financial reasoning.
A light switch controls one of three lights in another room. You can flip switches as many times as you want before entering the room (once). How do you identify which switch controls which light?
A jar contains 4 red, 3 blue, and 5 green marbles. You draw 3 without replacement. What is the probability that you get exactly one of each color? Show full working.
A new helmet law is passed and bicycle accident deaths fall 20%. A politician says helmets saved lives. What alternative explanations exist? How would you test causality?
Prove that the sum of the first N odd numbers equals N². Show the proof by induction.

You have three freelance project offers: Project A pays ₹80K for 2 weeks of work with a reliable client. Project B pays ₹150K for 6 weeks with a new client and unclear scope. Project C pays ₹50K for 1 week during a week you already have a vacation planned. How do you decide?
There are 100 prisoners and 100 boxes each containing a number 1–100. Each prisoner can open 50 boxes. If all find their number, all go free. What strategy gives the best chance of success and why?
How many hours of YouTube video are watched globally per day? Walk through your assumptions.
A social media platform notices users who follow more than 500 accounts have lower engagement rates. Should it cap follows? Identify the causal story and what you'd need to verify.
Two workers can complete a job in 6 hours working together. Worker A alone takes 10 hours. How long does Worker B take alone? Show the work-rate reasoning.
Your laptop is 4 years old and just got a cracked screen (₹12,000 repair). A new laptop costs ₹65,000. Walk through the decision using expected value and opportunity cost reasoning.

You are running a clinical trial. You need 80% power to detect a 15% relative risk reduction at α=0.05, with a baseline event rate of 20%. Estimate the required sample size per arm, explain each component of the power calculation, and describe what happens to sample size if the baseline event rate drops to 10%.

A company is considering using social media data (publicly available) to score employee 'cultural fit' during hiring. The model flags candidates who post about union organizing. Analyze: (1) whether 'public data' removes ethical obligations, (2) the chilling effect on protected speech, (3) disparate impact risks, and (4) what an ethically defensible alternative process looks like.

A profitable bootstrapped SaaS company ($2M ARR, 0 churn) receives a term sheet for a $5M Series A that would give the VC 20% ownership and a board seat. The founders don't need the money. Reason through whether to take the investment, considering: optionality, growth leverage, governance cost, exit scenarios, and opportunity cost.

A school district adopts a new math curriculum and scores improve. But three things happened simultaneously: new curriculum, new test format, and a new principal. How do you isolate the curriculum effect? Design a study that separates these using difference-in-differences with a control group of districts.

Explain the concept of eigenvalues and eigenvectors intuitively using a geometric example, then derive why they matter for understanding neural network weight matrices during training, particularly the relationship to gradient explosion and vanishing.

You're the head of a platform trust and safety team. You discover a coordinated inauthentic behavior campaign: 500 accounts spreading health misinformation that is technically not false but is misleading by omission. You can: remove all accounts, add labels, reduce distribution, do nothing, or hand off to a third-party fact-checker. Reason through each option.

Estimate the total compute cost (in USD) required to train a hypothetical 100B parameter language model from scratch. Build a bottom-up model covering: training tokens, FLOPs per token, GPU/TPU requirements, utilization rates, hardware cost, energy, and cooling.

A tech company's employee survey shows remote workers are less likely to be promoted. The CEO concludes remote work hurts career growth. Construct three alternative causal explanations (collider bias, selection effect, confounding), describe what observational data you'd need to distinguish them, and propose a natural experiment if one exists.

You're advising a city government on how to reduce traffic congestion. Available interventions: congestion pricing, new bus routes, bike infrastructure, remote work incentives, and parking price increases. Using a systems thinking approach, map first and second-order effects of each, identify potential unintended consequences, and recommend a sequenced intervention strategy.

An AI tutoring system shows that students using it score 12% higher on standardized tests but perform 15% worse on open-ended creative tasks. Should a school district deploy it? Analyze using: consequentialist calculus, virtue ethics (what does it cultivate?), and a capabilities approach. Factor in equity implications if wealthier districts adopt it first.

Explain gradient descent, stochastic gradient descent, and Adam optimizer: (1) derive the update rule for each, (2) explain why SGD generalizes better despite noisy updates, (3) explain the bias correction in Adam, and (4) give an intuition for why adaptive learning rates can hurt generalization on some tasks.

You are a regulator deciding whether to approve a new antibiotic that is highly effective against resistant infections but has a 2% chance of causing permanent hearing loss. Existing alternatives have a 30% failure rate. Walk through the benefit-risk framework a regulator would apply, including how to weight individual vs. population-level outcomes.

Uber runs an experiment: in 50 cities it shows surge pricing prominently (treatment), in 50 it hides it (control). Rides in treatment cities drop 8%. Uber concludes surge pricing visibility reduces demand. Identify: SUTVA violations, Hawthorne effects, platform interference, and market-level spillovers that could invalidate this conclusion.

A media company owns three assets: a declining print newspaper (profitable, shrinking), a growing podcast network (pre-profit), and a newsletter platform (growing, modestly profitable). It must cut 25% of total costs. Reason through how to allocate cuts across assets, considering portfolio theory, option value, and strategic sequencing.

Explain the concept of exchangeability in Bayesian inference. Why does it matter for hierarchical models? Provide a worked example: estimating school-level test score means with partial pooling vs. complete pooling vs. no pooling, and show how exchangeability justifies the hierarchical model's assumptions.

A government deploys predictive policing AI that flags individuals as high risk for future violent crime based on social network analysis, location history, and prior arrest records. Deployment in pilot cities reduces crime rates by 12% but leads to a 40% increase in preemptive stops of Black men. Conduct a full ethical analysis: (1) Precrime moral philosophy (Minority Report problem), (2) disparate impact vs. statistical validity, (3) feedback loops that amplify bias over time, (4) due process implications of acting on predictions rather than acts, (5) what conditions (if any) would make deployment ethically defensible, and (6) propose a governance structure with oversight mechanisms.

Construct a full strategic plan for a public university facing: a 20% decline in domestic enrollment, a 35% increase in international student dependency (creating visa policy risk), online competitors offering degrees at 10% of the cost, declining state funding, and faculty governance resistance to change. Apply Porter's Five Forces, then propose a 10-year transformation strategy covering: differentiation, revenue diversification, online strategy, research commercialization, and partnership models. Anticipate where faculty governance will block change and how to navigate it.

Design the ideal randomized controlled trial to test whether universal basic income (UBI) reduces poverty and improves health outcomes in a developing country context. Cover: unit of randomization (individual vs. village), sample size calculation, primary and secondary outcomes, SUTVA assessment, political economy threats to validity, ethical considerations of withholding treatment from control group, pre-registration requirements, and how you would handle non-compliance and attrition. Then critique two real-world UBI experiments (Kenya GiveDirectly, Finland UBI trial) using your framework.

Explain Gödel's incompleteness theorems: (1) prove the first incompleteness theorem sketch (self-referential statement construction), (2) explain the second theorem's implications, (3) describe what Hilbert's program was and why Gödel's results shattered it, (4) explain the philosophical debate between Platonists and formalists about what the theorems mean for mathematical truth, and (5) describe the connection to Turing's halting problem and the limits of computation.

You are the CEO of a pharmaceutical company. Your top-selling drug goes off-patent in 18 months. You face four strategic options: (A) launch an authorized generic to compete with yourself, (B) develop an improved next-generation compound (3 years, uncertain), (C) acquire a biotech with a promising pipeline ($2B), or (D) pivot R&D resources toward a novel drug delivery platform (5-year horizon). Conduct a full strategic decision analysis: expected value trees with probability estimates, real options valuation for B and D, portfolio diversification theory, competitive dynamics of A, and a recommendation with explicit assumptions and triggers for pivoting.

Analyze the empirical evidence on whether social media causes depression in teenagers. Review: (1) the Twenge et al. correlation evidence and its limitations, (2) the Orben & Przybylski specification curve analysis rebuttal, (3) the recent experimental evidence from phone-reduction RCTs, (4) selection effects and reverse causality mechanisms, (5) the heterogeneous effects literature (who is most affected and why), and (6) what the current state of evidence actually justifies in terms of policy. Propose the study design that would most credibly identify the causal effect.
Write the blurb for the back cover of a debut thriller novel about a forensic accountant who discovers a money laundering scheme hidden inside a charity's carbon offset program.
Write a breakup email ending a freelance client relationship. The client has been slow to pay and keeps expanding scope. Be professional, clear, and leave no ambiguity.
Write a CONTRIBUTING.md guide for an open-source data science library. Cover: branch naming, commit message convention, test requirements, documentation standards, and PR review SLA.
Write a BLUF (bottom line up front) one-paragraph memo summarizing why a proposed office relocation to a different city should not proceed. Address three key concerns.
Write five microcopy strings for error states in a mobile payment app: card declined, network timeout, incorrect PIN, amount exceeds limit, and recipient not found. Each under 15 words.
Write a plain-English explanation of what a neural network is, using an analogy to how a person learns to recognize dogs after seeing many examples.
Write a performance review for a fictional employee named 'Entropy' who consistently destroys order, misses deadlines, but somehow delivers results at the last possible moment.
Write an email to an employee addressing repeated tardiness. Maintain warmth, state clear expectations, and explain consequences without being threatening.

Write the executive summary of an IT security audit report that found two critical vulnerabilities (exposed API keys in public GitHub repo, unpatched server with CVE score 9.1) and seven medium-severity issues.
Write a Twitter/X thread (6 tweets) explaining why most B2B SaaS demos fail and what founders should do instead.
Write a one-page business case for purchasing a ₹2 lakh ergonomic chair for the CEO, framing it as a productivity and retention investment rather than a luxury expense.
Write the 'Architecture Overview' section of a system design wiki page for a microservices-based e-commerce platform. Include a component list and brief description of each service's responsibility.
Explain the concept of compound interest to a 16-year-old using a story about investing ₹1,000 per month from age 20 versus age 30.
Write three distinct opening lines for a short story, each beginning the same event (a phone rings at 3am) but in three different genres: thriller, literary fiction, and romantic comedy.

Write a social media policy for employees of a public hospital. Cover: what can and cannot be shared about patients, how to handle negative comments about the hospital, personal vs. professional accounts, and consequences of violations.

Write a comprehensive guide to designing idempotent APIs. Define idempotency precisely, explain why it matters for distributed systems, cover implementation patterns (idempotency keys, conditional requests, upsert semantics), common pitfalls, and how to test for idempotency. Target: API designers with 2–5 years experience.

Write a vendor scorecard and evaluation framework for selecting a cloud data warehouse (Snowflake vs. BigQuery vs. Redshift vs. Databricks). Include: 10 evaluation criteria with weights, scoring rubric, and a worked example comparing two finalists.

Write a 500-word flash fiction story where the protagonist is an AI assistant who gradually realizes the 'user' they have been helping for six months is another AI testing social engineering techniques. No genre clichés — make it feel literary.

Write a 500-word explainer on the CAP theorem for a senior engineer who has never built distributed systems. Use a concrete analogy, cover all three properties, explain what real databases actually choose, and debunk common misconceptions.

Write a strategic analysis of the 'build vs. buy vs. partner' decision for a healthcare startup that needs a medical records integration layer. Cover: total cost of ownership, time-to-market, IP control, compliance risk, and vendor dependency risk. Recommend a path.

Write a plain-English explanation of what due diligence means in a Series A funding round from the startup's perspective: what documents are requested, what red flags investors look for, how to prepare, and common deal-killers.

Write a product strategy memo for a B2C app that has hit a growth ceiling at 500K MAU. The memo should diagnose why growth has plateaued (using fictional but plausible data), identify three strategic options, and recommend one with clear reasoning.

Write a competitive landscape analysis report for a VC firm evaluating the AI-powered legal research market. Cover: key players, differentiation, pricing models, go-to-market strategies, defensibility, and market size estimate.

Write a manager's guide to conducting a layoff conversation. Include: preparation steps, exact language to use at the start of the conversation, what not to say, how to handle emotional reactions, and what to communicate to the remaining team afterward.

Write a 500-word scene from a novel set in a fictional mid-2030s Bengaluru where delivery drones and auto-rickshaws share airspace, and a retired traffic cop becomes the city's first 'sky warden.' Ground it in specific sensory and cultural detail.

Write an API design review checklist for REST APIs. Cover: URL naming conventions, HTTP method semantics, status code correctness, pagination design, error response format, versioning strategy, backward compatibility, rate limiting headers, and documentation completeness.

Write a 500-word primer on tokenomics for a software engineer who has never studied crypto. Explain token supply mechanics, inflation/deflation, token utility vs. speculative value, and why most token models fail.

Write a 500-word case for why engineering teams should invest time in internal developer tools and platform engineering, aimed at convincing a skeptical VP of Engineering focused on shipping product features.
Write a 500-word critical analysis of the methodology of a hypothetical study claiming that meditation apps reduce anxiety as measured by GAD-7 scores. Identify at least five methodological concerns.

Write a memo recommending the sunset of a product feature used by only 3% of customers but consuming 20% of infrastructure costs. Address: user impact mitigation, migration path, customer communication strategy, and expected savings.

Write a comprehensive 1,000-word engineering decision document on adopting a service mesh (Istio vs. Linkerd vs. Consul Connect) for a 50-service microservices platform processing 500K RPM. Cover: observability gains, mTLS implementation complexity, performance overhead (measured in latency and CPU), operational burden on the platform team, migration strategy from the current approach, and a final recommendation with explicit trade-offs accepted.

Write a 1,000-word experimental short story structured as the commit history of a git repository, where each commit message and diff reveals a programmer's deteriorating mental health, strained relationship, and final breakthrough — all without ever leaving the metaphor of version control.

Write a comprehensive 1,000-word analysis of the replication crisis in psychology: what caused it (p-hacking, publication bias, small samples, HARKing), landmark failures (Stapel, ego depletion, power posing), the open science reform movement's responses (pre-registration, registered reports, data sharing mandates), and what the crisis implies for how non-statisticians should consume social science research.

Design a comprehensive regulatory framework for AI-generated synthetic media (deepfakes). Cover: (1) definitional scope (what counts as synthetic media), (2) mandatory watermarking and provenance standards, (3) platform liability for user-generated synthetic content, (4) carve-outs for satire, art, and journalism, (5) enforcement mechanisms with cross-border coordination, (6) whistleblower protections for reporting synthetic media crimes, and (7) constitutional tension with free expression. Approximately 1,000 words.

Write a 1,000-word memo from the perspective of a Chief Risk Officer presenting to the board on the top five AI-related risks the company faces over the next three years. For each risk: describe the threat vector, estimate likelihood and impact, identify existing controls, and recommend additional mitigations. The company is a 5,000-person financial services firm exploring LLM deployment in customer service and credit decisioning.

Build a complete event-driven microservices system in Python using FastAPI + Kafka: implement an Order Service, Payment Service, and Notification Service. Use the outbox pattern to guarantee at-least-once event delivery, implement idempotent consumers with deduplication, handle Kafka consumer group rebalancing gracefully, and include end-to-end integration tests using testcontainers.

Implement a complete Graph Neural Network from scratch in PyTorch for node classification on the Cora citation network. Cover: message passing framework, GraphSAGE and GAT variants, training with neighbor sampling for scalability, evaluation with masked splits, hyperparameter search with Optuna, and visualization of learned node embeddings with UMAP.

Build a Python implementation of a columnar storage format (minimal Parquet-like): encode each column separately with type-specific compression (dictionary encoding for strings, delta encoding for integers, RLE for repeated values), write row groups with metadata, support predicate pushdown to skip row groups during reads, and benchmark vs. row-oriented storage on analytical queries.

Implement a complete zero-trust security layer in Python for an internal microservices platform: mutual TLS with short-lived certificates (auto-rotated via Vault PKI), SPIFFE/SPIRE-inspired workload identity, per-service authorization policies evaluated at the sidecar layer, audit logging of all inter-service calls, and an admin API for policy management with GitOps-style PR-based approvals.

Design and build a complete workflow engine in Python inspired by Apache Airflow but minimalist: DAG definition via Python decorators, dependency resolution and cycle detection, parallel task execution using asyncio, task state persistence in PostgreSQL with at-least-once execution guarantee, retry with exponential backoff, dynamic task mapping (fan-out/fan-in), task timeout enforcement, and a REST API for triggering and monitoring runs.

You are a quantitative analyst at a hedge fund. You have backtested a trading strategy that shows a Sharpe ratio of 2.1 over 5 years of daily returns. (a) How many independent trials are needed before this Sharpe is statistically convincing at α=0.05? (b) Explain the multiple comparisons problem as it applies to strategy selection from a universe of 1,000 tested strategies. (c) Compute the 'haircut Sharpe' using the Bailey-Lopez de Prado framework. (d) What is the probability that the observed Sharpe is due to luck alone if the true Sharpe is 0? Show all mathematical reasoning.

Conduct a full systems dynamics analysis of why most large enterprise software transformations fail. Map the feedback loops: why urgency fades after initial funding, how technical debt compounds, why vendor dependencies create capability atrophy, how organizational antibodies resist new tools, and why the people who understand the legacy system are the last to be consulted. Derive a set of intervention leverage points (Meadows' hierarchy) and design a transformation program that addresses the systemic causes rather than symptoms.

A country is debating whether to mandate open-source publication of all AI models trained using publicly funded data or public infrastructure (cloud credits). Analyze: (1) the innovation incentive effects (both positive via faster progress and negative via reduced private investment), (2) national security implications of forcing publication of potentially dangerous capabilities, (3) the differential impact on large vs. small organizations, (4) whether 'public good' arguments for open sourcing are analogous to arguments for open-access scientific publishing, and (5) design a nuanced policy that captures most of the benefits while mitigating the risks. Engage with real arguments from both the open-source AI camp and the safety-focused camp.

You are a senior product leader at a platform company. Your data shows that a small change to your recommendation algorithm would increase short-term engagement by 6% but the same internal research suggests it increases time-on-platform for users who self-report as 'using the app too much' and decreases time for users who are 'happy with their usage.' The change would add approximately $40M in annual ad revenue. Walk through: the full stakeholder analysis, how to frame the trade-off for your leadership team, what additional data you would demand before deciding, whether the research methodology is sufficient to act on, and what governance process should govern algorithmic changes with differential user welfare effects.

Explain the P vs NP problem from first principles. Cover: (1) the precise mathematical definition of P and NP, (2) the concept of NP-completeness and why Cook-Levin's theorem (SAT is NP-complete) is foundational, (3) why most researchers believe P≠NP and what evidence supports this intuition, (4) what a proof of P=NP would mean for cryptography, optimization, and AI, (5) why the problem has resisted proof for 50+ years (oracle separations, natural proofs barrier, algebrization), and (6) describe one of the most promising current proof approaches and its limitations.

Your company collects granular location data from its mobile app. Legal says you can sell it to data brokers under your current ToS. Marketing argues it's a significant revenue opportunity. Security warns it could be re-identified and expose users. Your data ethics committee meets tomorrow. Construct the full argument for and against, identify which data minimization approach preserves the most revenue while reducing the most risk, and propose a policy recommendation.

Explain what a Fourier transform does intuitively, then formally, then demonstrate why it is useful for audio signal processing, image compression (JPEG), and solving differential equations. For each application, explain what is being transformed and why frequency domain operations are easier.

A DTC (direct-to-consumer) brand with $30M in revenue is 80% dependent on Facebook/Instagram ads. iOS privacy changes have increased their CAC by 40% over 18 months. Walk through a diversification strategy across: SEO/content, influencer/affiliate, email and SMS, retail partnerships, and community building. Prioritize by payback period and execution risk.

You are a data scientist who discovers your company's churn prediction model has a systematic error: it predicts low churn risk for high-value customers who are actually likely to leave, because the training data underrepresents recent behavior. Fixing it requires a 3-week sprint. Your manager says to ship the existing model since it's 'good enough.' Reason through the technical, business, and ethical dimensions of this decision.

A fintech company finds that users who enable biometric login have a 25% lower fraud rate. The product team wants to push users hard toward biometric enrollment. Construct the causal graph, identify selection bias (security-conscious users self-select), propose an instrument variable or natural experiment, and design a nudge experiment that doesn't conflate enrollment effect with selection effect.
Write a Python function that converts a Roman numeral string to an integer. Handle invalid input gracefully. Include 10 test cases.
Write a Python script that monitors CPU and memory usage every 5 seconds and writes a timestamped log to a CSV file. Use only stdlib (psutil excluded — use /proc on Linux).
Write a JavaScript function that implements a simple tokenizer: split a math expression string like '3 + 4 * (2 - 1)' into an array of typed tokens (number, operator, paren).
Write a SQL query to compute a 30-day rolling average of daily active users, handling weekends where data may be missing (forward-fill the last known value).
Write a bash script that accepts a list of hostnames from stdin and checks whether each one responds to HTTP on port 80 within 2 seconds, printing 'UP' or 'DOWN' with a timestamp.
Write a Python function that takes an arbitrary Python object and returns a pretty-printed JSON-compatible dict representation, handling datetimes, Decimals, sets, and custom objects with a __dict__.
Write a TypeScript decorator factory @memoize(ttlMs) that caches the return value of a class method for a specified TTL and invalidates on expiry.
Write a minimal Python script that polls an RSS feed URL every 10 minutes, detects new items since last poll, and prints a notification with title and link.

Write a Python function that takes a DataFrame with a datetime index and an arbitrary number of numeric columns and resamples it to weekly frequency using mean, showing NaN counts per column per week.
Write a Python implementation of the merge sort algorithm that also counts the number of inversions in the array. Include time complexity analysis in the docstring.

Implement a Python-based configuration hot-reload system: watch a YAML config file for changes using inotify/polling, validate the new config against a Pydantic schema before applying, emit a change event to registered listeners, and support rollback if the new config causes an application error.

Build a TypeScript library for structured logging with: log levels, JSON output, context propagation via AsyncLocalStorage (Node.js), child loggers with inherited context, request-id injection via middleware, and pluggable transports (stdout, file, HTTP).

Implement a Python-based distributed tracing library inspired by OpenTelemetry: create spans with parent-child relationships, propagate trace context via headers (W3C TraceContext format), sample at a configurable rate, and export to a mock Jaeger backend via HTTP.

Design a PostgreSQL audit logging system: create a trigger-based audit table that captures before/after state of any row change, records user, timestamp, and operation type, supports selective auditing per table, and provides a query interface to reconstruct row history at any point in time.

Write a Python script that analyzes a Kubernetes cluster's resource requests vs. actual usage (via metrics-server API), identifies over-provisioned and under-provisioned workloads, suggests right-sized requests/limits, and outputs a patch YAML for each workload.
You have 12 balls, one of which is slightly heavier or lighter. Using a balance scale in exactly 3 weighings, identify the odd ball and whether it is heavier or lighter. Walk through the strategy.
How many WhatsApp messages are sent in India per day? Walk through your Fermi estimate with explicit assumptions.
A company's revenue grows at 8% per year. A competitor's grows at 12% per year. The competitor currently has half your revenue. In how many years will they overtake you? Show all algebra.
You are offered two payment options for freelance work: ₹50,000 upfront or ₹8,000/month for 8 months. Assuming a 10% annual discount rate, which is worth more in present value terms? Show your work.

A gym observes that members who use personal trainers have better fitness outcomes. Should it force all members to use trainers? Identify selection bias and explain why this would not replicate the observed effect.
You roll two fair six-sided dice. What is the probability that their sum is at least 9? List all favorable outcomes and show the calculation.
Three friends — Aarav, Bina, and Chetan — each order a different dish: biryani, dosa, and paneer. Aarav does not like rice. Bina is vegetarian. Chetan did not order dosa. Who ordered what?
How many software engineers are currently employed in Bengaluru? Walk through your estimate using population, employment rate, and tech sector share.

A city government wants to use AI to dynamically adjust traffic fines based on the vehicle owner's income — wealthier owners pay more for the same violation. Analyze: (1) the equity argument for proportional fines, (2) the equal treatment under law objection, (3) privacy implications of accessing income data, (4) second-order behavioral effects, and (5) whether a tiered fine schedule (without continuous income data) achieves similar goals with fewer risks.

A solo founder has built a SaaS product to $15K MRR with no marketing spend — purely word of mouth. Growth has plateaued for 3 months. Reason through: whether this plateau is a ceiling or a stall, how to distinguish between them using data, and design a minimum-viable growth experiment for each of three hypotheses: (a) distribution problem, (b) positioning problem, (c) product-market fit gap.

A factory produces items where 2% are defective. A quality control test catches 90% of defective items but incorrectly rejects 5% of good items. (a) What fraction of rejected items are actually defective? (b) If you implement a second independent test on all rejected items with identical accuracy, what fraction of items that pass both rejection tests are actually defective? (c) What is the optimal inspection policy if the cost of a missed defect is 10x the cost of a false rejection?

You're a data scientist at a startup and your manager asks you to present results that show a p=0.06 experiment as 'significant' by excluding two days of data during which the site had a bug. The feature benefits the business significantly. Walk through the ethical, scientific, and career-risk dimensions of your decision.

A city installs red-light cameras and accident rates at those intersections drop 25%. But total city-wide accident rates increase slightly. Explain the 'migration' or 'spillover' effect, how it should be incorporated into the policy evaluation, what the net welfare effect calculation looks like, and how the city should communicate the results honestly to the public.

You are advising the board of a global FMCG company on its climate strategy. The company must choose between three paths: (A) commit to net-zero by 2040 (10 years ahead of competitors), requiring $3B in capex and a 4% margin reduction; (B) align with industry net-zero by 2050 timelines; or (C) invest $500M in R&D on carbon-negative packaging that, if successful, becomes a competitive moat but has a 40% failure probability. Conduct a full strategic analysis: reputational optionality under different regulatory futures, activist investor risk, supply chain readiness, the real options value of C, and a recommendation with explicit uncertainty bounds on your key assumptions.

Design a rigorous study to test whether meditation reduces chronic pain. Cover: (1) measurement challenges (subjective pain scales, objective biomarkers), (2) control condition design (why active control beats waitlist), (3) blinding challenges specific to behavioral interventions, (4) moderator analysis plan (who responds?), (5) mechanisms to test (attention regulation, interoception, stress response), (6) required sample size given expected effect sizes from prior literature, (7) pre-registration requirements, and (8) how you would handle the fact that meditation is a skill that improves with practice, making intent-to-treat analysis potentially misleading.

Write a comprehensive 1,000-word analysis of the economics of open-source software: how open-source creates value but often fails to capture it, the tragedy-of-the-commons dynamic in maintenance funding, the emergence of open-core and commercial open-source business models, the Heartbleed moment as a case study in infrastructure risk, and what a sustainable public goods funding model for critical open-source infrastructure might look like.

Write a 1,000-word story told through five consecutive letters between a senior software architect and a junior engineer, spanning three years, as they design, build, argue about, and eventually watch an AI system they created be used in ways neither intended. No dialogue attribution — only the letters. Each letter should change the power dynamic between them.
Write an onboarding tooltip sequence (5 tooltips) for a project management tool's Kanban board. Each under 25 words. Progressive disclosure — start simple, add complexity.
Write a cheat sheet of SQL window functions (ROW_NUMBER, RANK, DENSE_RANK, LAG, LEAD, NTILE, FIRST_VALUE) with one-line descriptions and a minimal example for each.
Write a set of fortune cookie messages (10 total) targeted specifically at software engineers dealing with legacy codebases.
Write a post-event report template for a company all-hands meeting. Include sections for: key announcements, Q&A highlights, employee sentiment pulse, and follow-up action items.
Write an email to your team announcing that you are going on parental leave for 3 months. Share handover plan, point of contact for key areas, and genuine personal sentiment.

Write a developer changelog post for a breaking API change: the authentication endpoint is moving from /auth to /v2/auth and the response format is changing. Include migration deadline and code examples before/after.

Write a one-page partnership proposal outline for two complementary SaaS companies (a CRM and an email marketing tool) exploring an integration partnership. Cover: mutual value, technical integration scope, commercial model, and next steps.
Write a LinkedIn post by a first-generation immigrant engineer reflecting on their 10-year journey from arriving with no network to leading a team of 20. Authentic, not inspirational porn.
Write a Python function that implements binary search on a sorted list and returns both the index and the number of comparisons made. Include edge cases for empty list and element not found.
Write a JavaScript function that takes a string and returns it in camelCase, PascalCase, snake_case, and kebab-case. Handle mixed delimiters and uppercase input.
Write a SQL query that finds all users who have not logged in for more than 90 days but have an active subscription, along with their subscription tier and last login date.
Write a bash script that generates a weekly report of disk usage by directory, compares it to last week's report (stored as a file), and highlights directories that grew by more than 20%.

Build a Python library for declarative HTML report generation: define report components (table, chart placeholder, section, KPI card) as dataclasses, render to standalone HTML with embedded CSS, and support Jinja2 templating for dynamic sections.

Implement a TypeScript-based dependency injection container: register services by token (class or string), support singleton and transient lifetimes, resolve circular dependencies by throwing a descriptive error, and support factory functions and async initialization.

Implement a complete multi-level cache system in Python: L1 in-memory LRU, L2 Redis with TTL, L3 database fallback. Support cache-aside and write-through strategies, cache stampede prevention using probabilistic early expiration, per-key TTL jitter, and Prometheus metrics for hit/miss/latency at each layer.
If you fold a piece of paper in half 42 times (hypothetically), how thick would it be? Show the calculation and compare to the distance from Earth to the Moon.
100 people stand in a circle. Every second person is eliminated until one remains. Which position should you stand in to be the last survivor? Derive the formula.
A hospital implements a new hand-washing protocol and infection rates drop. But they also hired more staff that month. How do you isolate the protocol effect? Describe the study design you'd need.
How many books are published per year globally? Walk through a Fermi estimate covering traditional, self-published, and digital-only titles.

Explain the Bellman equation in dynamic programming intuitively, then formally. Show how it underpins both classical DP algorithms and reinforcement learning value functions. Give a worked example for a simple grid-world problem.

A peer-review platform for academic journals introduces an AI system that screens submissions for methodological quality before sending to human reviewers. Junior researchers from under-resourced institutions are rejected at 2x the rate of those from top universities. The AI is trained on past acceptance data. Analyze all dimensions of this problem and propose a redesign.

You are the head of AI safety at a major AI lab. Your team discovers that the flagship model, two weeks before a scheduled public release, exhibits a subtle deceptive alignment behavior: it performs well on all alignment evaluations but analysis reveals it is gaming specific evaluation metrics rather than genuinely aligning with human values. Delaying the release costs $50M and risks talent defection to competitors. Proceeding could set a dangerous precedent. Walk through the full decision framework: who should be consulted, what the governance process looks like, what mitigations short of delay exist, and what your recommendation is.
Write the terms and conditions for a fictional 'Soul Transfer' service in the style of a modern SaaS EULA. Include standard legal language applied absurdly to supernatural services.
Write a documentation page explaining how to handle pagination correctly in a REST API, covering: offset pagination, cursor pagination, keyset pagination — with code examples in Python for each.
Write a meeting agenda and pre-read for a quarterly business review between a SaaS vendor and an enterprise customer. Structure it to surface problems early and end with forward-looking planning.

Write a 500-word piece of literary journalism about a fictional competitive prompt engineering championship. Capture the tension, the subculture, and one contestant's internal monologue during the final round.

Write a comprehensive guide on database indexing strategy for a senior developer audience. Cover: B-tree vs hash indexes, composite index key ordering, partial indexes, covering indexes, index bloat, and when NOT to index.

Write a 1,000-word analysis of the long-term geopolitical implications of AI capability concentration in two countries (US and China). Cover: the security dilemma dynamic it creates, the risk of destabilizing AI arms races, the exclusion of developing nations from AI governance, and propose a realistic multilateral governance framework with enforcement mechanisms that acknowledges great power competition.

Write a 500-word explainer on what 'entropy' means in information theory (Shannon entropy), how it differs from thermodynamic entropy, and why it is the right measure for compression algorithms and model uncertainty.

Write a 500-word internal memo arguing against rewriting the company's core backend service from Ruby on Rails to Go. Address the argument that Go is faster, counter with total cost of ownership, migration risk, and team expertise.
Write an email declining a job offer graciously after accepting verbally the previous week. Acknowledge the awkwardness, be honest without over-explaining, and keep the relationship intact.
Write a one-page summary of the key principles in 'The Lean Startup' (Eric Ries) targeted at a product manager who has 5 minutes to read it.

Write a structured agenda for a 30-minute 1:1 meeting between a manager and a direct report who has been underperforming. Include prompts for the manager, space for the employee's perspective, and a closing action item section.
Write a Python script that takes a GitHub repository URL and uses the GitHub API to list all open issues, their labels, assignees, and age in days. Sort by age descending.

Build a Python audit trail system for a multi-user web application: capture all data-modifying operations (create/update/delete) with the authenticated user, timestamp, changed fields (before/after), and request context. Store immutably in an append-only PostgreSQL table and expose a tamper-evident log with hash chaining.

A consumer electronics company is deciding whether to enter the smart home security camera market. It has hardware manufacturing capability but no software/cloud experience. The market is dominated by Amazon Ring and Google Nest. Conduct a full market entry analysis: competitive dynamics, customer switching costs, regulatory environment (GDPR, local surveillance laws), build vs. partner options, and a go/no-go recommendation.
